newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX gasoline takes up baton of strength.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX gasoline takes up baton of strength.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
*Gasoline looks likely to take up the baton of strength.
*Crude's gains are seen slowing with the markets upside momentum running out of steam and technicals mostly neutral.
*Technicals are seen continuing to support heating oil but trading ranges are expected to narrow down as the market heads into the seasonal doldrums and stocks start to build.

NYMEX crude and heating oil markets are seen stable to firmer in the short term and while crude's upside is slowing and analysts still seen room for heat to improve, only gasoline looks likely to take up the baton of strength, analyst and traders said.

Despite the belief shared by many that crude prices are too high, the gasoline market has been unable to sustain any sort of downward move and the structure of the board has moved into backwardation, suggesting nearby tightness.
Traders said uncertainty over political situations in key producing nations and scattered refinery troubles this week were also keeping gasoline sellers at bay.

"There are a lot of shorts in June, in the June/July (spread), and the June heat-to-gas spread. The (DOE) stats were bullish. We've got stocks under last year's total and the driving season right around the corner", one trader said.

On Wednesday a bid of $21.86 for 1,000 lots of July crude from one investment bank was said to have triggered a strong wave of short covering which spiked the market. Also supportive were weekly inventory figures showing stocks fell by over 5 million barrels.
However, analysts are sceptical of further gains with the upside momentum running out of steam and technicals mostly neutral.
"If we don't hit $22.50 (basis July) very soon, then the top has been put in," said one unimpressed oil company analyst.

"I think we're probably running out of time," she said. "There are too many people out there ready to sell $22 crude. There's a lot of crude and product around, and U.S. refiners can crank out as much gas as they need for the season. I can't get too excited on the upside here."
Technical indictors showed historic volatility staying very low at around 18.7 and 20.6 percent for 10- and 20-day measures respectively.

Technicals were seen continuing to support the heating oil market but trading ranges are expected to narrow down with prices easing as the market heads into the seasonal doldrums and stocks start to build.
However, a doji candlestick on Wednesday's front-month continuation chart is signalling a brake of the market's recent dip from the highs and some players feel the market still has room to move up.
"This contract is the strongest of the market and so we watch carefully to see if it leads us higher, away from a test of support", MeesPierson said in its daily energy report.
